We killed our AI strategy last quarter.

Not because it failed. Because nobody could say what it was for.

Six slides, two vendors, one steering committee. Zero customers had asked for any of it.

So we replaced the deck with a single question: which task did a person do twice this week that a machine should have done once?

Three answers came back. We built the smallest one first.

It shipped in nine days and saves the support team about four hours a week. Small, boring, real.

Strategy is the word people use when they have not picked a task yet.
